name: Indian Railway Finance Corporation Ltd.
business_summary: Government-owned (82.9%) borrowing arm of Indian Railways: raises funds from bond, term-loan and external markets and leases rolling stock and infrastructure assets to the Ministry of Railways on finance leases priced at its borrowing cost plus a thin ~0.40% spread, giving near-zero credit risk (zero NPA) and no tax for several years. Q2 FY27 PAT Rs1,958cr (+10.2% y/y), revenue +23.5% (lease income growth), finance costs Rs5,917cr (vs Rs4,544cr). FY27 borrowing programme up to Rs70,000cr, of which Rs24-28k cr ECBs. Diversifying into non-railway lending (HURL refinancing Rs12,800cr; loan book aiming to cross Rs1 lakh cr). Stock Rs80, -34% over 12m, -24.9% over 6m, near 52-week lows; interim dividend Rs1.15.

revenue_mix.segment: Lease income from Ministry of Railways
Loans to other PSUs/infra (HURL, etc.), interest and other income

exposures.mechanism: Earnings are insulated (cost-plus lease: lease rate = borrowing cost + ~0.40% spread, set by Ministry of Railways), so yields barely move PAT. Equity sensitivity is via (1) refinancing: ~Rs0.3 lakh cr/yr of maturities and Rs70,000cr new borrowing at higher coupons raise lease income AND interest equally (spread unchanged), (2) valuation: a bond-proxy PSU yield stock (interim dividend Rs1.15 on Rs80 = 1.4% for the half-year) loses relative appeal when 10y goes 7.4-7.5%. +25bp => -1.0. Stock -34% over 12m already.

evidence.note: India 10y G-sec ~7.4-7.5% in Oct 2026, multi-year high (Reuters/ET headlines); Nov outlook 7.25-7.35%
Q2 FY27 PAT Rs1,958cr +10.2%, interim dividend Rs1.15; finance cost Rs5,917cr vs Rs4,544cr

exposures.mechanism: Borrowings ~Rs4.7 lakh cr (model estimate) mostly fixed-rate bonds/term loans (floating ~15%); lease rates reset annually and pass through. +25bp: ~Rs0.7 lakh cr floating x 0.25% = Rs175cr gross, passed through within months => residual lag cost ~Rs30cr = 0.4% of PAT x persistence 0.5; rating AAA. -0.4.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (The Hindu, Reuters headlines)
cost-plus lease model, spread ~0.40%, disbursement target Rs35,000cr

exposures.mechanism: Borrowing programme Rs70,000cr in FY27 (35-40% via ECBs): spreads widen funding cost, passed through in lease rate but spread is capped at ~0.40%; wider spreads raise rollover risk and slow disbursement growth (target Rs35,000cr). +50bp spreads on new Rs70,000cr = Rs350cr annual interest passed through; residual margin squeeze/volume effect ~-0.8.

evidence.note: FY27 borrowing up to Rs70,000cr, ECB Rs24-28k cr

exposures.mechanism: Railways capex funds extra-budgetary resources via IRFC: +10% capex plan => IRFC disbursement +~5% => assets and PAT +~4% over 2 yrs (margin 0.4% on a larger book) x persistence 0.5 on an equity (PAT) basis, not EV, because debt is passed through to the lessee => +1.5. IRFC share of railway funding is shifting (budgetary support rising, EBR falling) - key long-run driver.

evidence.note: cost-plus lease model, spread ~0.40%, disbursement target Rs35,000cr

exposures.mechanism: IRFC is diversifying into non-railway loans (HURL refinancing Rs12,800cr; loan book targeted to cross Rs1 lakh cr in FY27); higher infra spending expands PSU-borrower pipeline. +10% => +~0.6.

ECB share 35-40% of FY27 borrowings (Rs24-28k cr) and ~Rs1.2 lakh cr of foreign-currency debt (model estimate), fully hedged or passed through to the Railways under lease rate resets; unhedged residual / hedging cost spikes at INR 94.5. +3% USD/INR => hedging cost + sentiment => -0.5. Pack: -1.89 (t -0.8), not significant; agrees on sign.

evidence.note: FY27 borrowing up to Rs70,000cr, ECB Rs24-28k cr

exposures.mechanism: PSU high-beta (1.5-1.6) stock; retail/F&O-driven. VIX +5 => Nifty -3.5% => beta ~1.55 => -5%, ~85% removed by demeaning; residual stock-specific high-beta effect -0.6. Not in empirical top-12.

FIIs hold only 1.15% (promoters 82.9% after OFS in Q1 FY27: 84.65% -> 82.90%); flows are minor. +US$5bn/qtr => +3% Nifty x beta 1.6 => ~+4.8% market effect, mostly demeaned; PSU-bond-proxy dampens => +0.8.
Retail ownership 12% and DII 4% (up from 2.9% in Mar 2026 as DIIs absorbed the OFS); SIP/DII +10% supports PSU small-cap demand; +1.0.

Central capex, of which railways is a large component, drives IRFC disbursement; +10% capex growth => IRFC disbursement +4% => PAT +~3% over 2yrs x 0.5 => +1.2. Overlaps with P_RAILWAY_CAPEX (De-duplicate: use the railway edge for rail-specific changes).
Tight liquidity (Oct 2026 RBI measures) raised bond yields; surplus liquidity eases primary-market borrowing costs by ~5bp on Rs70,000cr = Rs35cr, passed through; mostly valuation support => +0.4.
